name: Caer Arianrhod

attributes.attribute: said to have had relations with mermen
linked to a rock off the coast of Wales

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Caer Arianrhod is a Welsh mythological site. The name also appears as Caer Aranrhod. It was the great castle of Arianrhod, a goddess of the Mabinogion. A great flood destroyed the castle. Some writers blamed the people who lived there. They describe this as a late and Christian way of reading the goddess. She was said to have had relations with mermen. A rock near the Welsh shore may mark the ruin. It lies about a mile out to sea. Other sources say the castle was carried up into the sky.

okr.objective: Caer Arianrhod is the great flooded castle of the Welsh goddess Arianrhod.
